title: Som Tam
subtitle: Thai green papaya salad with lime, fish sauce, and chilli
excerpt: Som tam is Thailand's most popular salad: shredded unripe green papaya pounded with garlic, chilli, lime juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and tomatoes. It is simultaneously sour, salty, sweet, and hot. The pestle and mortar bruises the ingredients rather than crushing them; the texture is the point.
sourceNotes: Som tam (literally sour pounded) originated in Laos and Northeast Thailand (Isan) and became the national salad of Thailand. The papaya used is unripe, green, and crunchy; it has almost no flavour of its own and acts as a vehicle for the dressing. It is traditionally made to order in a clay mortar. The dish spread globally from the 1980s onwards.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten immediately. The papaya softens as it sits.

content.text: Peel and shred the green papaya using a julienne peeler or the coarse holes of a box grater; you want thin, long strips. Green papaya is available from Asian supermarkets. Use the pestle to bruise rather than pulverise: the strips should be lightly crushed, not turned to mush.

items.prepNote: peeled and shredded into thin strips
bird's eye chilli; adjust to taste

content.text: Pound the garlic and chilli in a large pestle and mortar to a rough paste.
Add the green beans and cherry tomatoes. Pound lightly to bruise but not crush.
Add the shredded papaya. Pound and turn with a large spoon simultaneously: pound to bruise the strips, use the spoon to lift and fold.
Mix the lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar until dissolved. Pour over the salad and toss. Taste: adjust the balance of lime (sour), fish sauce (salt), and sugar (sweet) to your preference.

items.cause: Papaya was over-pounded or left sitting in the dressing
items.fix: Pound lightly and serve immediately. The papaya releases water as it sits.
